races.title: State Assembly, District 2
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Chris Rogers
cands.bio: Democrat who has represented California's 2nd Assembly District since December 2024. Former Santa Rosa mayor (2020–2022) and city councilmember (elected 2016). Earlier worked in U.S. Rep. Lynn Woolsey's district office and as a senior staffer to State Sen. Mike McGuire.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Teachers Association, California Nurses Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action, among others, for the 2026 election.

cands.gaps: We found no recorded stance from Rogers on data centers, homestead property taxes, investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, guns, police pay, or school choice. His planks on development and land are thin, and we found no documented stance on specific development projects. His claim of balancing Santa Rosa's budget as mayor comes from his own survey response, and we found no independent report of it. We found no controversies, foreign ties or Ballotpedia 2026 survey responses.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born and raised in Sonoma County, and his campaign site and Ballotpedia survey response say he was born and raised on the North Coast, where he still lives in Santa Rosa.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2024 (Budget Committee among his assignments), Santa Rosa mayor 2020–2022, councilmember from 2016, former staffer to a U.S. Representative and a state senator, with a Master's in Public Administration.
qual.why: He has held a legislative seat and led a city as mayor and councilmember. He also has policy staff experience with a state senator and public administration training. His state legislative tenure is short, so he scores in the high range rather than the top.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site says he is working to restore salmon habitat, prevent wildfires, advance conservation and expand access to open space.

cands.name: Michael Greer
cands.bio: Republican candidate for Assembly District 2. Retired special education teacher and transition specialist. Member of the Del Norte County Unified School District board (District 5). Says he was Paradise Unified School District board president during the Camp Fire and was elected to the Gridley town council at 27. Ran for this seat in 2024 and 2026.

endorsements.text: Reform California, the California Rifle and Pistol Association and several Northern California officials, including Congressman James Gallagher, Sen. Meghan Dahle and former Sen. Brian Dahle, are listed in his own Ballotpedia survey answers. Ballotpedia separately lists Reform California as an endorser.

His campaign site lists endorsements from Steve Hilton (candidate for governor), Sen. Meghan Dahle, Sonja Shaw (candidate for Superintendent of Public Instruction), Rep. James Gallagher, the late Rep. Doug LaMalfa and Carl DeMaio of Reform California.
The Republican Party of California endorsed him in 2024, per Ballotpedia.

cands.gaps: We found no votes or official actions by Greer on data centers, property taxes, land ownership, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. His campaign materials stay general on affordability, accountability, education restructuring and local control, and water storage, and none of them speak to those issues directly. His birthplace, where he grew up, and when he first came to California are not stated in the sources. Dates for his Gridley council and Paradise school board service were not given. His claims of 20+ years of lobbying and teachers' union presidency come only from his own site, and no independent records or reporting were available. No news coverage or controversies about him were found.

local.label: Roots 55: He earned a Chico State degree in 1999, says he served on the Gridley council and the Paradise school board, and has lived in Del Norte County about six years, so the record shows him living in California as an adult for 25+ years; his birthplace and upbringing are not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Local elected office: school boards in Del Norte County and (by his account) Paradise, where he says he was board president, and a Gridley town council seat. Retired special education teacher and teachers' union president. His site claims 20+ years of lobbying in Washington and Sacramento.
qual.why: Middle band for a record of local elected office and a long education career. He has no legislative or state budget experience, and the lobbying claim is self-reported and unverified.
